# Overview {#sec-overview}

"Habitat suitability" (HS) here refers to the daily feeding response of a species [0-1]. Originally, habitat suitability was going to me measured via two mechanisms: feeding response and metabolic response (catabolism at half-weight - anabolism). This was simplified to just feeding response for a few reasons:

1. By its nature, catabolism - anabolism includes feeding response in its calculation, meaning that feeding response is double-counted when both measures are used.
2. Since catabolism always increases with temperature (albeit by different slopes) all the interesting changes in HS come from changes in the feeding response.
3. When placed side by side, it is very difficult to tell (visually) if there are any significant differences in HS from the two measures.

This document calculates habitat suitability for all 16 model species within the EEZ areas of all countries currently producing marine fed mariculture.

# Species parameters {#sec-species-params}

```{r load-parameters}
#| code-summary: 'Load species parameters for all models'

params_files <- file.path(prepdata_path, "species_parameters") %>% 
  list.files(full.names = T)

model_names <- params_files %>% 
  basename() %>% 
  str_remove_all("species_parameters_|.qs")

parameters_species <- map(params_files, qd_read) %>% 
  setNames(model_names)

# Feed parameters
feed_params <- file.path(prepdata_path, "feed_parameters") %>% 
  list.files(full.names = T)

feed_names <- feed_params %>% 
  basename() %>% 
  str_remove_all(".qs")

feed_params <- map(feed_params, qs_read) %>% 
  setNames(feed_names)

model_names <- names(parameters_species)
```

# Habitat suitability per country/species

```{r temperatures-and-seacells}
#| code-summary: Get all the necessary data

EEZ_by_FAO_full <- file.path(prepdata_path, "EEZ_data_with_FAO_regions.qs") %>%
  qd_read() %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  st_make_valid()

data_source <- if (str_detect(here(), "/mnt/rdsi")) {rdsi_path} else {bigdata_path}

tos_rast_fnms <- file.path(rdsi_path, "raw_data", "ESGF", "EC-Earth3P-HR", "projected_adjusted") %>% 
  list.files(full.names = T) %>% sort()

tos_dates <- str_extract(basename(tos_rast_fnms), "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")
```

HS is calculated per country (EEZ), per species (model_name), per harvest year, and per day. The annual habitat suitability is then calculated as the sum of all days. 

```{r}
country_dirs  <- unique(EEZ_by_FAO_full$ISO3_Code)
harvest_years <- 2037:2064

inds          <- str_detect(tos_dates, paste0(harvest_years, collapse = "|"))
tos_rast_fnms <- tos_rast_fnms[inds]
tos_dates     <- tos_dates[inds]
```

Habitat suitability is calculated for all species in all countries, even if that species is not currently farmed there. This is in case we want to go back to that - in the consolidation phase, only species actually grown in each country will count towards the overall habitat suitability score.

```{r reference-raster}
#| code-summary: "Create a binary EEZ-union mask raster"
#| eval: false

# Rasterise the union of all EEZs onto the SST grid so we can mask ocean cells outside any EEZ to NA before running the model.
ref_rast <- rast(tos_rast_fnms[1])
ref_crs  <- crs(ref_rast)

sf_use_s2(FALSE)
eez_union <- EEZ_by_FAO_full %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%      # GEOS make_valid can handle the crossing rings
  st_union() %>%
  st_as_sf()
sf_use_s2(TRUE)            # restore the default for later operations

eez_union_v <- project(vect(eez_union), ref_crs)
eez_mask    <- rasterize(eez_union_v, ref_rast, field = 1)  # 1 inside EEZ, NA outside
rm(ref_rast, eez_union, eez_union_v); gc()
```

```{r save-habitat-suitability-global}
#| code-summary: "Main harvest year → species global habitat suitability loop"
#| eval: false

HS_global_dir <- here("outputs/data/habitat_suitability/global")

# ── Create all filenames & directories ─────────────────────────────────────
# One row per species × year × metric (FR = feeding rate, MR = metabolic rate);
# only rows whose file is missing are kept, so a year is skipped entirely if
# both files exist, and only the missing metric is calculated otherwise.
files_HS_global <- expand_grid(model_names, harvest_years, metric = c("FR", "MR")) %>%
  mutate(
    filename = file.path(HS_global_dir, model_names, paste0(metric, "_", harvest_years, ".tif")),
    exists   = file.exists(filename)
  ) %>%
  filter(!exists)

for (d in unique(dirname(files_HS_global$filename))) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

files_HS_global <- split(files_HS_global, files_HS_global$harvest_years)

# ── Feed parameters used for metabolism ───────────────────────────────────
# Several species have more than one feed; the first listed feed is used here.
feed_for_species <- map(
  set_names(model_names),
  function(sp) {
    nm <- str_subset(feed_names, paste0("^", sp, "-"))[1]
    if (is.na(nm)) stop("No feed parameters found for ", sp)
    feed_params[[nm]]
  }
)

# ── Raster wrapper for get_metabolism() ───────────────────────────────────
# get_metabolism() is scalar (uses if()/min()), so it is evaluated once per
# unique temperature (rounded to `digits`) and the results are looked up for
# every cell/day, rather than calling it per cell.
# The overfeeding draw in food_prov_rate() is made deterministic for this
# application by setting overFdelta = 0, so rnorm() returns overFmean exactly.
get_metabolism_r <- function(temp_stack, species_params, feed_params, digits = 2) {
  species_params["overFdelta"] <- 0

  temp_vec <- as.vector(terra::values(temp_stack))
  ok       <- is.finite(temp_vec)

  temp_round  <- round(temp_vec[ok], digits)
  temp_unique <- sort(unique(temp_round))
  mr_unique   <- vapply(
    temp_unique,
    function(tt) unname(get_metabolism(
      water_temp     = tt,
      species_params = species_params,
      feed_params    = feed_params,
      rep_size       = species_params[["CS"]]
    )),
    numeric(1)
  )

  full     <- rep(NA_real_, length(temp_vec))
  full[ok] <- mr_unique[match(temp_round, temp_unique)]

  r <- terra::setValues(temp_stack, matrix(full, nrow = terra::ncell(temp_stack), ncol = terra::nlyr(temp_stack)))
  names(r) <- names(temp_stack)
  r
}

# ── MAIN LOOP ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# files <- files_HS_global[[1]]
# yr_char <- names(files_HS_global)[1]
walk2(
  files_HS_global,
  names(files_HS_global),
  function(files, yr_char) {
    if (nrow(files) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))

    # 1. Read SST for this year (only now that we know at least one file is missing)
    this_tos_fnms    <- tos_rast_fnms[str_detect(tos_dates, yr_char)]
    tos_stack_global <- rast(this_tos_fnms)

    # Apply the EEZ-union mask so that open ocean == NA
    suppressWarnings(tos_stack_global <- tos_stack_global * eez_mask)

    # 2. Calculate and save only the missing species × metric files
    pwalk(
      files,
      function(model_names, metric, filename, ...) {
        resp_global <- if (metric == "FR") {
          get_feeding_responses_r(
            temp_stack     = tos_stack_global,
            species_params = parameters_species[[model_names]]
          )[["feeding_response"]]
        } else {
          get_metabolism_r(
            temp_stack     = tos_stack_global,
            species_params = parameters_species[[model_names]],
            feed_params    = feed_for_species[[model_names]]
          )
        }

        # 3. Sum across days to get a single-layer global raster and save
        resp_global <- app(resp_global, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
        writeRaster(resp_global, filename, overwrite = TRUE)
        rm(resp_global); gc()
      }
    )
    rm(tos_stack_global); gc()
  },
  .progress = T
)
```

The global rasters are then cropped and masked to each country's EEZ.

```{r save-habitat-suitability-country}
#| code-summary: "Split global habitat suitability rasters into per-country files"
#| eval: false

HS_global_dir <- here("outputs/data/habitat_suitability/global")
HS_dir        <- here("outputs/data/habitat_suitability")

# ── Pre-project EEZ polygons to raster CRS ────────────────────────────────
ref_crs   <- list.files(HS_global_dir, pattern = "\\.tif$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)[1] %>% rast() %>% crs()
EEZ_vects <- EEZ_by_FAO_full %>%
  split(.$ISO3_Code) %>%
  map(~ vect(.x) %>%
        aggregate(by = "ISO3_Code") %>% # combine all fishing regions into a single EEZ per country
        project(ref_crs))

# ── Build job table: one row per global file (FR and MR) × country ────────
jobs <- tibble(
  global_file = list.files(HS_global_dir, pattern = "^(FR|MR)_\\d{4}\\.tif$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
) %>%
  mutate(
    model  = basename(dirname(global_file)),
    fname  = basename(global_file),
    metric = str_extract(fname, "^(FR|MR)")
  ) %>%
  filter(model %in% model_names) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(iso = country_dirs) %>%
  mutate(country_file = file.path(HS_dir, iso, model, fname))

todo <- filter(jobs, !file.exists(country_file))
message(nrow(todo), " of ", nrow(jobs), " country files to create")

walk(unique(dirname(todo$country_file)), dir.create, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ── Read each global file once, then crop/mask per country ────────────────
todo_grp <- todo %>%
  summarise(iso = list(iso), country_file = list(country_file), .by = global_file)

pwalk(
  todo_grp,
  function(global_file, iso, country_file) {
    HS_global <- rast(global_file)
    walk2(iso, country_file, function(i, fnm) {
      eez_v <- EEZ_vects[[i]]
      crop(HS_global, eez_v) %>%
        mask(eez_v) %>%
        writeRaster(fnm, overwrite = TRUE)
    })
  },
  .progress = T
)
```

Habitat suitability is then saved per country EEZ, per species, and per decade (manually defined). Since it would be way too many plots to show HS (or relative change in HS) over all production years, instead we're going to save absolute HS in each decade and relative change in HS compared to the reference.

We also decided to save HS in "global warming levels" using the corresponding periods defined in [Table 1 here](https://climatedata.ca/resource/introduction-to-global-warming-levels/).

```{r decadal-HS}
#| code-summary: Calculate (absolute) decadal mean HS rasters per country and species

decades <- list(
  "ref_2015_2024" = 2015:2024,
  "dec_2020_2029" = 2020:2029,
  "dec_2030_2039" = 2030:2039,
  "dec_2040_2049" = 2040:2049,
  "dec_2050_2059" = 2050:2059,
  "dec_2060_2069" = 2060:2069,
  "dec_2070_2079" = 2070:2079,
  "dec_2080_2089" = 2080:2089,
  "dec_2090_2099" = 2090:2099,
  "GLW_1.5" = 2018:2037,
  "GLW_2.0" = 2032:2051,
  "GLW_3.0" = 2055:2074,
  "GLW_4.0" = 2075:2094
)

HS_dir     <- file.path(outs_path, "data", "habitat_suitability")
HS_dec_dir <- file.path(outs_path, "data", "habitat_suitability_decadal")

# One job per country × model × metric (FR/MR) × decade
jobs <- map(
  set_names(country_dirs),
  function(iso) {
    HS_files <- list.files(file.path(HS_dir, iso), full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE, pattern = "^(FR|MR)_\\d{4}\\.tif$") %>% sort()
    if (length(HS_files) == 0) return(NULL)

    by_group <- tibble(
      file   = HS_files,
      model  = basename(dirname(HS_files)),
      metric = str_extract(basename(HS_files), "^(FR|MR)"),
      year   = as.integer(str_extract(basename(HS_files), "\\d{4}(?=\\.tif$)"))
    ) %>%
      group_split(model, metric)

    map(by_group, function(g) {
      tibble(
        iso      = iso,
        model    = g$model[1],
        metric   = g$metric[1],
        dec_name = names(decades),
        in_files = map(decades, \(d) g$file[g$year %in% d])
      )
    }) %>% list_rbind()
  }
) %>%
  list_rbind() %>%
  filter(lengths(in_files) > 0) %>%   # drop decades with no files
  mutate(out_file = file.path(HS_dec_dir, iso, model, paste0(metric, "_", dec_name, ".tif")))

todo <- filter(jobs, !file.exists(out_file))
message(nrow(todo), " of ", nrow(jobs), " decadal files to create")

walk(unique(dirname(todo$out_file)), dir.create, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

walk2(
  todo$in_files,
  todo$out_file,
  function(in_files, out_file) {
    rast(in_files) %>%
      app("mean", na.rm = TRUE) %>%
      writeRaster(filename = out_file, overwrite = TRUE)
  },
  .progress = T
)
```

# Re-consolidate habitat suitability

Finally, we narrow down the HS files to those that we actually want to plot. For now, we're going to look at:

- The species that are actually grown in each country
- The GLW levels, relative to today
